scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: It's the IT department office here (our machines are
the 192.168.1.x ones). None of our computers can get to anything on the
network any more -- not the shared drives, not the other departments,
nothing, and it hit all of us at the same time. A whole room does not go
dark together on its own. Someone here said it plainly: the department
switch has died. I wouldn't know which box that is or where it lives, but it
is your box and your job to find it. Check whatever connects our room to the
rest of the campus and get us back on today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: None observed at the network layer. The IT VLAN (192.168.1.0/24), its access switch, and the default gateway are operating normally.
- Mechanism: End-to-end IP connectivity from IT hosts to other departments and servers is intact. We validated L2 within the IT LAN, L3 to the gateway, and routed reachability to multiple remote subnets.
- Localization: IT LAN on switch0 (br0 with eth1=lan_it and eth0=uplink to router0) and router0.eth0 (192.168.1.1). Links are up with link-detected=yes on switch0 eth0/eth1 and router0 eth0. Router0 has correct routes to all remote networks.
- Evidence:
  • it_hod (192.168.1.2) can ping: gateway 192.168.1.1, peer it_lab1 (192.168.1.3), office_pc (192.168.3.2), principle pc0 (192.168.4.2), servers pc1 (1.0.0.5), internet VLAN pc2 (128.168.0.2) – all 0% loss.
  • it_lab1 shows identical healthy reachability.
  • switch0 is bridging correctly (br0 up; eth0/eth1 up; link detected yes).
  • router0.eth0 is up at 192.168.1.1 with RIP-learned routes to 192.168.3.0/24, 192.168.4.0/24, 128.168.0.0/16, 1.0.0.0/8.
- Root cause: The reported IT-wide outage is not reproducible now; no failed switch or gateway is found—likely a transient or non-network-layer issue (e.g., server/DNS hiccup or brief upstream flap).
- Corrective fix: No network changes required. Service is currently restored. Recommend: verify name resolution and shared-drive server health if users still report issues; monitor switch0 and router0 interfaces for flaps, and collect timestamps if the symptom recurs.
